docs.title: DataGEMS Query Recommender Api
docs.text:
This is the documentation site for the DataGEMS Query Recommender Api. The service is part of the wider DataGEMS platform. This is part of the overall platform documentation.

The Query Recommender Api suggests what a user might want to ask next. Given the natural language query the user has just submitted, it returns up to 3 short follow-up queries, personalised with the user's interest keywords as maintained by the User Profiler service. The suggestions are generated by a Large Language Model (LLM) served by the DataGEMS LLM endpoint.

A typical exchange looks like this:

POST /api/v1/recommend-next-queries
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "current_query": "What is there to do in Verona tonight?",
  "context": { "user_id": "user1" }
}

{
  "next_queries": [
    "Concerts in Verona this weekend",
    "Opera at the Arena di Verona",
    "Late night restaurants in Verona"
  ]
}

You can use the menu options on the left to navigate through the available documentation. You may be interested to jump directly to an Architecture Overview, see the available Onboarding Material, read about some Api Constructs, investigate how to interpret Status & Error Codes or jump straight in to the OpenAPI Reference. You can find the repository for the service here: code repository.

For any questions, you can consult the FAQ, check if there is a relevant issue answering your question or contact the DataGEMS Help Desk.

docs.title: Api Overview
docs.text:
The service exposes a small HTTP Api under the /api/v1 prefix. In the DataGEMS development deployment it is reachable at https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/qr/api/v1. All request and response bodies are JSON.

The full, machine readable description is available in the OpenAPI Reference. A running instance also serves it at:

  • /api/v1/openapi.json: the OpenAPI document
  • /api/v1/swagger: Swagger UI
  • /api/v1/redoc: ReDoc

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Path Auth Description GET /api/v1 no Api root: confirms the Api is running and lists the endpoints POST /api/v1/recommend-next-queries yes Recommends the next queries for the current one POST /api/v1/authtest yes Checks that a bearer token is accepted by the service

GET / redirects to /api/v1.

docs.title: Recommend next queries
docs.text: POST /api/v1/recommend-next-queries

docs.title: Request
Response
Example
docs.text:
curl -X POST "https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/qr/api/v1/recommend-next-queries" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"current_query": "What is there to do in Verona tonight?", "context": {"user_id": "user1"}}'

docs.title: Auth test
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/authtest

Validates the caller's token in the same way as the recommendation endpoint (signature, issuer, expiry and audience) and echoes back the request and the identity found in the token. It is useful to check a token, or a client's authentication setup, without involving the LLM.

The request body has the same shape as the auth test endpoints of the other DataGEMS Apis. Both fields are required and no other fields are allowed:

{
  "query": "test",
  "k": 1
}

Response:

{
  "authorized": true,
  "message": "Token is valid",
  "request": { "query": "test", "k": 1 },
  "subject": "the subject id",
  "username": "the preferred username"
}

docs.title: Api root
docs.text:
GET /api/v1

Does not require authentication. Returns a short status message and the list of available endpoints:

{
  "message": "API V1 is running",
  "endpoints": {
    "recommend-next-queries": {
      "description": "Get the next queries given the previous one",
      "methods": ["POST"],
      "url": "/api/v1/recommend-next-queries",
      "example_url": "/api/v1/recommend-next-queries"
    },
    "authtest": {
      "description": "Test endpoint requiring a valid bearer token",
      "methods": ["POST"],
      "url": "/api/v1/authtest"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: The Api version is part of the path (/api/v1). Breaking changes to the request or response format will be introduced under a new path prefix.

docs.title: Service Architecture
docs.text: The Query Recommender is a small, stateless HTTP Api written in Python with FastAPI and served by uvicorn. It does not own a data store: every recommendation is computed on demand from the incoming request, the user's profile and an LLM call. Nothing is persisted between requests.

docs.title: Ecosystem
docs.text:
The service sits between the DataGEMS clients that want to offer "what to ask next" suggestions and two underpinning services:

  • DataGEMS AAI (Keycloak): issues the access tokens that callers present. The service downloads the realm's public keys (JWKS) to verify them. See Security.
  • User Profiler: holds each user's interest keywords, extracted from their past activity. The service reads them to personalise the suggestions.
  • LLM endpoint: an OpenAI-compatible chat completions Api (in the DataGEMS deployment, the one served at chat.scayle.es). It generates the suggestions.
                 ┌──────────────────────┐
  client ──────▶ │  Query Recommender   │ ──── JWKS ─────▶  DataGEMS AAI (Keycloak)
  (Bearer token) │       Api            │
                 │                      │ ── profile ────▶  User Profiler  (caller's token forwarded)
                 │                      │
                 │                      │ ── models ─────▶  LLM endpoint   /api/models
                 │                      │ ── chat ───────▶  LLM endpoint   /api/chat/completions
                 └──────────────────────┘

docs.title: Request flow
docs.text:
A call to POST /api/v1/recommend-next-queries goes through the following steps:

  1. Authentication. The bearer token is verified (signature, issuer, expiry) against the AAI public keys, then its audience is checked for the service's client id. Failures stop the request with 401, 403 or 503 as described in Status & Error Codes.
  2. User keywords. If the request context contains a user_id, the service calls GET {USER_PROFILER_API_URL}/user/{user_id}/profile, forwarding the caller's token, and takes the keywords of the profile. The User Profiler returns keywords strongest (most recently seen) first, and only the top 15 are kept. This step never fails the request: if there is no user_id, the user is unknown (404), the token is rejected (401/403), or the profiler is unreachable, the recommendation is generated with no keywords.
  3. Model selection. The service lists the models available at the LLM endpoint (/api/models, on the same host as the chat endpoint) and uses the preferred model (llama-3.3) if it is there, otherwise the first model listed. If the list cannot be retrieved, it tries the preferred model name as is.
  4. Generation. The LLM receives a system prompt asking for 3 short next search queries, close to the current one but not repeating it, favouring the most relevant keywords, plus a user message with the current query and the keywords. The reply is requested as JSON of the form {"queries": [...]}, constrained with a JSON schema response_format. If the LLM endpoint rejects response_format with a 400, the call is retried once relying on the prompt alone.
  5. Validation and clean-up. The reply is parsed (tolerating markdown fences or extra text around the JSON object) and validated against the expected shape. Queries are trimmed, and empty ones, duplicates and repeats of the current query (case-insensitive) are dropped. At most 3 are returned.
  6. Response. The service answers 200 OK with {"next_queries": [...]}. If the LLM could not be reached, or its reply was not valid, it answers 502 Bad Gateway instead.

The caller's token is only ever forwarded to the User Profiler. The LLM endpoint is called with the service's own LLM token.

docs.title: Code layout
docs.text:
The service code lives in the query-recommender repository:

  • qr_api/main.py: the FastAPI application, the Api root and the router mounting under /api/v1
  • qr_api/resources/endpoints.py: the recommend-next-queries endpoint
  • qr_api/resources/security.py: token validation and the authtest endpoint
  • qr_api/resources/user_tools.py: the User Profiler client
  • qr_api/resources/LLM_tools.py: model selection, prompt, LLM call and reply validation
  • qr_api/resources/data_models.py: the request and response models
  • qr_api/tests/: sample request payloads
  • app.py: a Streamlit chat demo that calls the Api, described in Onboarding

docs.title: Automations
docs.text: A number of automations are available to facilitate the development, deployment and documentation of the service. Here we describe the ones that are directly, publicly available.

docs.title: Dockerfile
docs.text: The main delivery package for the service is a docker image. The Dockerfile at the root of the code repository builds the Docker image. Dependencies are installed with uv from the committed uv.lock, so the image always contains the exact dependency versions that were tested.

docs.title: Docker image publishing
docs.text:
A GitHub Action workflow is available to build and publish the docker image for the service. The action is triggered when a new tag matching v* is pushed to the repository. This way, all the images produced are always named and can be traced back to the codebase snapshot that generated them.

The generated docker image is pushed to the GitHub organization Packages using the name of the service repo and the version tag that triggered the execution.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
A GitHub Action workflow is available to generate the documentation presented here. The action is triggered manually and runs against the head of the repository. The documentation generated is versioned and the documentation version is expected as input to the workflow.

The documentation is built using the mkdocs library and specifically using the Material for mkdocs theme. A number of additional tools are utilized, such as mike to support versioning and neoteroi.mkdocsoad to support OpenAPI specification rendering.

The documentation is generated and tagged with the provided version, which is also aliased as latest. It is uploaded to a dedicated documentation branch that the repository GitHub Page presents its contents from.

The OpenAPI Reference is rendered from the openapi.json file kept with the documentation. When the Api changes, this file should be refreshed from a running instance (/api/v1/openapi.json) before publishing a new documentation version.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The service is configured entirely through environment variables. They are read once, when the service starts, so any change requires a restart.

docs.title: LLM
docs.text: Variable Default Description LLM_API_URL (none, required) Full URL of the OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint, e.g. https://chat.scayle.es/api/chat/completions. The list of available models is read from /api/models on the same scheme, host and port LLM_TOKEN (none, required) Bearer token used to call the LLM endpoint. This is a secret LLM_SSL_VERIFY true TLS certificate verification for the LLM endpoint. true verifies against the system CAs, a file path verifies against that CA bundle or certificate, false disables verification (for an endpoint with a self-signed certificate). With false, the service prints a warning at startup

docs.title: User Profiler
docs.text:
Variable Default Description USER_PROFILER_API_URL http://localhost:8000 Base URL of the User Profiler Api, used to fetch the users' interest keywords. In the DataGEMS cluster this is http://user-profiler-service:5000

If the User Profiler is not reachable at this URL, recommendations are still produced, without personalisation.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Variable Default Description OIDC_ISSUER_URL https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/oauth/realms/dev The expected token issuer (iss claim), i.e. the DataGEMS AAI realm OIDC_JWKS_URL {OIDC_ISSUER_URL}/protocol/openid-connect/certs Where the issuer public keys are fetched from OIDC_CLIENT_ID query-recommender The client id that must appear in the token audience (aud claim) JWKS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS 300 How long the public keys are cached, in seconds

See Security for how these are used.

docs.title: Http
docs.text:
Variable Default Description ROOT_PATH (empty) The path prefix under which a reverse proxy exposes the service, e.g. /qr. It is used so that the generated OpenAPI document and the Swagger UI work behind the proxy. The proxy is expected to strip the prefix before forwarding requests

The service listens on port 5000, both in the Docker image and when started with python -m qr_api.main.

docs.title: Model
docs.text: The preferred model is llama-3.3. At each request the service checks it against the models listed by the LLM endpoint, and falls back to the first available model if it is not offered. The preferred model is currently set in code, not through configuration.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
export LLM_API_URL="https://chat.scayle.es/api/chat/completions"
export LLM_TOKEN="your-llm-token"
export USER_PROFILER_API_URL="http://localhost:8000"
python -m qr_api.main

$env:LLM_API_URL = "https://chat.scayle.es/api/chat/completions"
$env:LLM_TOKEN = "your-llm-token"
$env:USER_PROFILER_API_URL = "http://localhost:8000"
python -m qr_api.main

When working against an LLM endpoint with a self-signed certificate, save the endpoint's certificate once and point LLM_SSL_VERIFY to it, rather than disabling verification:

openssl s_client -connect <llm-host>:<port> </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 > llm.pem
export LLM_SSL_VERIFY="$PWD/llm.pem"

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: LLM_TOKEN is the only secret the service needs. It should not be stored alongside the other configuration values. In the DataGEMS deployment it is kept in Vault and exposed to the container through a Kubernetes secret, as described in Deployment.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: The service is part of the DataGEMS platform offered through an existing deployment, following the DataGEMS release and deployment procedures over a managed infrastructure. The purpose of this section is not to detail the deployment processes put in place by the DataGEMS team, but to give an overview of what the service needs to run.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
The service is offered as a Docker image through the DataGEMS GitHub Organization Packages, as ghcr.io/datagems-eosc/datagems-eosc/query-recommender:<version>. This process is described in the relevant Automations section.

The image is based on python:3.12-slim, installs the locked dependencies with uv and starts the Api with uvicorn on port 5000:

docker run -p 5000:5000 \
  -e LLM_API_URL="https://chat.scayle.es/api/chat/completions" \
  -e LLM_TOKEN="your-llm-token" \
  -e USER_PROFILER_API_URL="http://user-profiler:5000" \
  ghcr.io/datagems-eosc/datagems-eosc/query-recommender:<version>

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text:
In the DataGEMS development cluster the service runs in the univr namespace, as:

  • a Deployment query-recommender with a single replica, a readiness probe on TCP port 5000 and resource limits of 500m CPU and 2Gi memory
  • a ClusterIP Service query-recommender-service on port 5000
  • an Ingress routing https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/qr/... to the service, stripping the /qr prefix (ROOT_PATH is set to /qr accordingly). Proxy read and send timeouts are raised to 300 seconds to leave room for slow LLM replies
  • a VaultStaticSecret that syncs the LLM_TOKEN from Vault into the query-recommender-secrets Kubernetes secret

The manifests are maintained in the deployment repository of the service.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: In order for the service to operate properly, the needed configuration values must be set to match the environment that it must operate in. The needed configuration is described in the relevant Configuration section.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
For the service to be able to operate, its underpinning services must be available and accessible:

  • the DataGEMS AAI, to verify tokens. Without it, authenticated calls fail with 503
  • the LLM endpoint, to generate the suggestions. Without it, recommendation calls fail with 502
  • the User Profiler, to personalise the suggestions. Without it, recommendations still work, without personalisation

The Architecture section describes the ecosystem in which the service needs to operate.

docs.title: Status & Error Codes
docs.text:
The HTTP Api exposed by the service exposes restful endpoints to offer its functionality. These endpoints are documented using the OpenAPI specification and available for integrators to consult in the respective API section.

In this section, we describe further the HTTP Status Codes that the service may return and the error information that accompanies them.

docs.title: Status Codes
docs.text:
The service makes use of the following subset of HTTP Status Codes:

  • 200 OK - the request has succeeded
  • 401 Unauthorized - the request lacks valid authentication credentials: the token is missing, malformed, expired, has an invalid signature or was issued by another issuer
  • 403 Forbidden - the token is valid, but it was not issued for this service (its audience does not include the service client id)
  • 422 Unprocessable Content - the request body does not match the expected model, for example a missing current_query
  • 502 Bad Gateway - the LLM endpoint could not be reached, returned an error, or replied with output that is not in the expected format
  • 503 Service Unavailable - the public keys needed to verify the token could not be fetched from the identity provider
  • 500 Internal Server Error - an unexpected condition prevented the service from fulfilling the request

Authentication is checked before the request body, so a request with both a bad token and a bad body gets a 401 or 403, not a 422.

Failures of the User Profiler never produce an error: the service falls back to recommendations without user keywords, as described in the Architecture.

docs.title: Error responses
docs.text:
Error responses follow the standard FastAPI format: a JSON object with a detail property. For all status codes except 422, detail is a human readable message:

Status detail Cause 401 Not authenticated No Authorization: Bearer header on recommend-next-queries 401 Missing bearer token No Authorization: Bearer header on authtest 401 Invalid token Bad signature, wrong issuer, expired or malformed token 403 Token missing required audience: query-recommender The token audience does not include the service client id 502 The LLM could not be reached or returned an invalid response The LLM call failed or its reply could not be parsed 503 Could not fetch JWKS: ... The identity provider public keys are not reachable

For example:

{
    "detail": "Token missing required audience: query-recommender"
}

401 responses produced when the header is missing on recommend-next-queries also include a WWW-Authenticate: Bearer header.

docs.title: Validation errors
docs.text:
For 422 responses, detail is a list with one entry per problem found in the request. Each entry has a loc pointing at the problematic property, a msg describing the problem, a machine friendly type and the input that was received.

For example, a request to recommend-next-queries with an empty body object:

{
    "detail": [
        {
            "type": "missing",
            "loc": ["body", "current_query"],
            "msg": "Field required",
            "input": {}
        }
    ]
}

Or a request to authtest with an extra property:

{
    "detail": [
        {
            "type": "extra_forbidden",
            "loc": ["body", "limit"],
            "msg": "Extra inputs are not permitted",
            "input": 10
        }
    ]
}

docs.title: Bad Gateway
docs.text: A 502 means the request was valid and authenticated, but the recommendation could not be produced by the LLM. Possible causes are the LLM endpoint being down or unreachable, the LLM token being invalid, the selected model being unavailable, or the model replying with something that is not a JSON object of the form {"queries": [...]}. The exact cause is logged by the service (see Logging) but is not returned to the caller. As LLM replies vary between calls, retrying the request may succeed.

docs.title: Why did I get fewer than 3 suggestions?
docs.text: The LLM is asked for 3 suggestions, but the ones that are empty, duplicated, or identical to the query you sent are dropped. The list can therefore have fewer than 3 entries, or even be empty.

docs.title: Why do I get different suggestions for the same query?
docs.text: The suggestions are generated by an LLM, which is not deterministic. The user's keywords can also change between calls, as the User Profiler updates them.

docs.title: Are the suggestions personalised?
docs.text: Only if the request context contains a user_id known to the User Profiler, and the token you send is also accepted by the User Profiler. Otherwise, the suggestions depend on the current query only. See Security.

docs.title: Does the service use the results of my query?
docs.text: Not yet. The context object accepts any additional fields, but only user_id is used at the moment.

docs.title: Does the service remember my previous queries?
docs.text: No. The service is stateless. Your past behaviour is taken into account only through the interest keywords maintained by the User Profiler.

docs.title: I get a 403 with "Token missing required audience"
docs.text: Your token was issued for another client. Request a token whose audience includes query-recommender.

docs.title: Known Issues
docs.text:
• A suggestion is not checked against the queries the user already made, so following the suggestions can lead back to a previous query.
  • The LLM call has no timeout of its own: a slow LLM endpoint makes the request slow too, up to the timeout of the client or of the ingress.
  • GET / redirects to /api/v1 without taking the proxy prefix into account. Behind the DataGEMS ingress, use /qr/api/v1 directly.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: The service writes its logs to standard output, where they are collected by the container runtime. In the DataGEMS cluster they can be read with the usual Kubernetes tooling, e.g. kubectl logs -n univr deployment/query-recommender.

docs.title: Access logs
docs.text:
Each request served is logged by uvicorn in its standard access log format, with the client address, method, path and status code:

INFO:     10.0.0.12:53124 - "POST /api/v1/recommend-next-queries HTTP/1.1" 200 OK

docs.title: Troubleshooting logs
docs.text:
The service logs the conditions that are handled without failing the request, or that are hidden from the caller behind a generic error:

Message Meaning JWT validation failed: ... A token was rejected (401). The message gives the reason, e.g. an expired signature User Profiler rejected the token (401/403): ... The User Profiler did not accept the forwarded token, so the recommendation was made without keywords. Usually means the token audience does not include the User Profiler Error while calling User Profiler API: ... The User Profiler could not be reached, so the recommendation was made without keywords Could not reach models endpoint: ... The list of available LLM models could not be fetched, so the preferred model name was used as is Error while calling API: ... The LLM call failed (502 to the caller) LLM reply contains no JSON object: ... The LLM replied without any JSON (502 to the caller). The reply is included LLM reply does not match the expected schema: ... The LLM replied with JSON of the wrong shape (502 to the caller) WARNING: TLS certificate verification for the LLM API is disabled ... Printed at startup when LLM_SSL_VERIFY=false

The service does not currently produce structured (JSON) logs, propagate a correlation identifier, or emit accounting entries.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text: The service is part of the DataGEMS platform offered through an existing deployment, following the DataGEMS release and deployment procedures over a managed infrastructure along with the maintenance activities that are scheduled within the platform. The purpose of this section is not to detail the maintenance activities put in place by the DataGEMS team.

docs.title: Healthchecks
docs.text:
The Api root, GET /api/v1, does not require authentication and answers 200 OK as soon as the service is up. It can be used as a liveness check:

curl https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/qr/api/v1

{ "message": "API V1 is running", "endpoints": { ... } }

This check does not cover the underpinning services. To also verify authentication end to end, call POST /api/v1/authtest with a valid token. To verify the LLM endpoint, a call to recommend-next-queries is needed.

In Kubernetes, the readiness of the container is checked with a TCP probe on port 5000.

docs.title: Versions & Updates
docs.text:
The service follows a semantic versioning scheme and structures versions as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH:

  • MAJOR (X.0.0): Breaking changes that are incompatible with previous versions.
  • MINOR (X.Y.0): New features added in a backward-compatible way.
  • PATCH (X.Y.Z): Bug fixes and security patches that do not affect compatibility.

Each version is released by pushing a vX.Y.Z tag, which builds and publishes the matching Docker image, as described in Automations.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text: The service is stateless and keeps no data of its own, so there is nothing to back up. The user profiles it reads are owned and backed up by the User Profiler.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Troubleshooting is primarily done through the logs, described in the respective logging section. Common symptoms and their usual causes are:

  • 401 on every call: the token is expired, or was issued by a different realm than OIDC_ISSUER_URL
  • 403 on every call: the token audience does not include query-recommender. The client must request a token for this audience
  • 502 on every call: the LLM endpoint is unreachable, LLM_TOKEN is wrong, or TLS verification is failing (look for CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED in the logs)
  • Recommendations work but are never personalised: look for User Profiler errors in the logs. Usually USER_PROFILER_API_URL is wrong, or the token is not accepted by the User Profiler

docs.title: Onboarding Material
docs.text: This section contains some references and material that will assist users and integrators onboarding process.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
The definite guide for integrators remains the service OpenAPI Reference.

The codebase is available under the MIT License in our GitHub code repository.

To get a better understanding of the endpoints and their payloads, you can read the Api Overview.

To know more about Api response codes and how to interpret them, you can take a look at the Status & Error Codes.

On aspects pertaining to security, you can read more at the Security section.

For an overall view of the service, you can go through the Architecture.

For any questions, you can consult the FAQ.

If you are facing a problem, check if there is a relevant issue answering your question.

You can always contact us through the DataGEMS Help Desk.

docs.title: Running locally
docs.text:
The service requires Python 3.10 or later. With uv:

git clone https://github.com/datagems-eosc/query-recommender.git
cd query-recommender
uv sync
export LLM_API_URL="https://chat.scayle.es/api/chat/completions"
export LLM_TOKEN="your-llm-token"
uv run python -m qr_api.main

The Api is then available at http://localhost:5000/api/v1, with the Swagger UI at http://localhost:5000/api/v1/swagger. See Configuration for all the settings, including how to point the service to a User Profiler.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Sample request payloads are available in the code repository, under qr_api/tests. They cover a request for a known user, a request without context and a request for an unknown user. To send one:

curl -X POST "http://localhost:5000/api/v1/recommend-next-queries" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @qr_api/tests/sample_query_1.json

$TOKEN must be an access token retrieved from the DataGEMS AAI service, with query-recommender in its audience.

docs.title: Demo application
docs.text:
The code repository includes a chat-style Streamlit demo, app.py. You type a natural language query, and the 3 recommended next queries are shown as buttons. Clicking one sends it as the next query.

pip install streamlit        # not included in the service dependencies
streamlit run app.py

In the sidebar you can:

  • choose the Api to use: local (http://localhost:5000/api/v1, overridable with the QR_API_URL environment variable), the remote development instance, or a custom URL
  • paste the Keycloak access token, sent to both the Query Recommender and the User Profiler. It can also be provided through the DATAGEMS_TOKEN environment variable. The demo warns when the token is missing or expired
  • pick a user from the User Profiler (local or remote development instance). The user's interest keywords are shown, and their id is sent as context.user_id. If the User Profiler is unreachable, a user id can be typed by hand
  • set the request timeout, check the Api status and clear the chat

docs.title: Quality Assurance
docs.text: Key aspects of the Quality Assurance checklist that DataGEMS services must pass have been defined in the processes and documents governing the platform development and quality assurance. In this section we present a selected subset of these that are directly, publicly available.

docs.title: Reproducible builds
docs.text: The service dependencies are pinned in the uv.lock file of the code repository, and the Docker image is built from that lock file (uv sync --frozen). Every published image is tagged with the version tag of the commit it was built from. See Automations.

docs.title: Output validation
docs.text: As the recommendations are produced by an LLM, the service does not trust its output. The LLM is asked to reply in a fixed JSON format, constrained with a JSON schema where the endpoint supports it. Every reply is then validated against that format, and the suggestions are cleaned (empty entries, duplicates and repeats of the current query are removed, and at most 3 are kept) before being returned. Replies that cannot be validated are reported to the caller as a 502 instead of being passed on. See Architecture.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Sample request payloads are kept in the code repository under qr_api/tests, covering a known user, a request without context and an unknown user. They can be sent to a local or deployed instance to smoke test it, as shown in Onboarding.

The Streamlit demo described in Onboarding can be used for manual, end to end testing against a local or deployed instance, including the User Profiler integration.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Key aspects of the Security checklist and practices that DataGEMS services must pass have been defined in the processes and documents governing the platform development and quality assurance. In this section we present a selected subset of these that are directly, publicly available and affect the usage and configuration of the service.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The recommend-next-queries and authtest endpoints require authentication using Bearer tokens in the form of JWTs (JSON Web Tokens). Clients must include a valid token in the Authorization header of each HTTP request, using the following format:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

The Api root (GET /api/v1) and the OpenAPI documentation endpoints are public.

The service only accepts JWTs issued by the trusted identity provider, the DataGEMS AAI service. When a token is received, the service:

  1. verifies the token signature with the public keys (JWKS) published by the issuer. Only RS256 signatures are accepted
  2. checks that the issuer iss claim matches the configured DataGEMS AAI realm
  3. checks the expiration exp claim, to confirm the token is still valid
  4. checks that the audience aud claim contains the client id of this service (query-recommender by default). aud can be either a single string or a list

Only if all these checks pass will the request be processed. A missing or invalid token results in 401 Unauthorized, while a valid token that was not issued for this service results in 403 Forbidden. If the public keys cannot be fetched from the issuer, the service answers 503 Service Unavailable. See Status & Error Codes for the response bodies.

The public keys are cached in memory for 5 minutes by default, so a key rotation at the issuer can take up to that long to be picked up.

You can check that a token is accepted by calling the POST /api/v1/authtest endpoint, described in the Api Overview.

The location of the configuration governing this behaviour is described in the relevant Configuration section.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text: There are no per-user permissions within the service. Any caller presenting a valid token with the right audience can request recommendations, for any user_id.

docs.title: Calls to other services
docs.text:
To personalise the recommendations, the service calls the User Profiler on behalf of the caller. It does so by forwarding the caller's access token as is, in the Authorization header. There is no token exchange: for personalisation to work, the token must also be accepted by the User Profiler, which means its audience must include the User Profiler client id as well. If the User Profiler rejects the token, the service logs the rejection and falls back to recommendations without keywords, so a misconfigured audience shows up as less personal suggestions rather than as an error.

The caller's token is never sent to the LLM endpoint. The LLM endpoint is called with a dedicated service token.

docs.title: TLS towards the LLM endpoint
docs.text: The service verifies the TLS certificate of the LLM endpoint against the system certificate authorities by default. This can be pointed to a specific CA bundle or certificate, or, for development against an endpoint with a self-signed certificate, disabled. Disabling verification prints a warning at startup. See Configuration.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: The LLM token is a secret and must be handled separately from the other configuration values. In the DataGEMS deployment it is kept in Vault and injected into the container as an environment variable. See Configuration and Deployment.
